entries.name: CesiumJS
entries.use_for: Render 3D globes and maps with terrain and 3D Tiles in the browser.
entries.why: The standard for web 3D geospatial; created the 3D Tiles format.
entries.summary: JavaScript library for 3D globes and 2D maps in the browser using WebGL, designed for dynamic data and 3D Tiles.
entries.best_for: Web 3D geospatial apps with terrain and 3D Tiles.
entries.not_for: Heavy for simple 2D maps; some data services require Cesium ion.

entries.name: deck.gl
entries.use_for: Visualize large geospatial datasets as GPU-accelerated layers over a map.
entries.why: Handles millions of points; integrates with MapLibre, Google Maps and React (vis.gl / OpenJS).
entries.summary: GPU-accelerated WebGL2/WebGPU visualization framework composing layers over maps for large datasets.
entries.best_for: Large-scale geospatial visualization with MapLibre, Google Maps or React.
entries.not_for: Visualization layer only; you need a basemap library, and it is overkill for a few markers.

entries.name: GDAL
entries.use_for: Read, write and convert raster and vector geospatial data in 200+ formats.
entries.why: The foundation of open GIS; nearly every geo tool (QGIS, PostGIS, rasterio) builds on it.

license_verified.note: LICENSE.TXT: GDAL/OGR in general MIT; some bundled parts under other licenses

entries.summary: Geospatial Data Abstraction Library for reading, writing and converting raster and vector data in 200+ formats.
entries.best_for: Geodata conversion and processing foundation, e.g. via Python or CLI tools.
entries.not_for: Large C++ toolkit with heavy install; not a web map renderer.

entries.name: GeoLibre
entries.use_for: Explore and analyze geospatial data in the browser, on desktop, mobile or in Jupyter.
entries.why: Offers 1,000+ geoprocessing tools that run in WebAssembly with data kept on your machine.
entries.summary: A free, cloud-native GIS platform built with Tauri v2 and React. It runs in the browser, on desktop and mobile, and inside Jupyter via a Python package. Over 1,000 tools for terrain, hydrology, LiDAR, remote sensing and vector analysis run in WebAssembly.
entries.best_for: A private, install-free GIS, or embedding map analysis into notebooks and apps.
entries.not_for: A full GIS app, not a mapping SDK for custom tile rendering. The README excerpt gives little detail on extending it.

entries.name: GeoPandas
entries.use_for: Work with geospatial vector data as pandas DataFrames.
entries.why: Core of the Python GIS stack: spatial joins, overlays, reprojection with a pandas API.
entries.summary: GeoPandas adds geographic data support to pandas through GeoSeries and GeoDataFrame types, subclasses of pandas Series and DataFrame. It works with shapely geometry objects for geometric operations, stores a coordinate reference system on objects, and reprojects with to_crs().
entries.best_for: Python geospatial analysis of vector data (points, lines, polygons) in a pandas-style workflow, including reading files and reprojecting CRS.
entries.not_for: Interactive web maps or raster processing. Geometry operations are cartesian, and like coordinates are not enforced across operations.

entries.name: God's Eye View
entries.use_for: Fork a browser-based 3D globe that shows live flights, ships, satellites, quakes and public cameras.
entries.why: Each data layer is a separate module, so you can add your own feeds.
entries.summary: God's Eye View puts public signals on one explorable photorealistic globe: flight transponders, ship beacons, orbital elements, seismographs and cameras. Features include click-to-track, cockpit view and sensor looks like thermal or night vision. It runs locally in the browser.
entries.best_for: You want a starting point or inspiration for a live geospatial visualization.
entries.not_for: License is unspecified (NOASSERTION). Some data is simulated or estimated, and photorealistic 3D needs a Cesium key.

entries.name: GraphHopper
entries.use_for: Compute routes, isochrones and distance matrices on OpenStreetMap data.
entries.why: Fast, mature open-source routing engine usable as a Java library or HTTP server.
entries.summary: Fast, memory-efficient routing engine on OpenStreetMap data, as Java library or web server, with turn-by-turn directions, snap to road and isochrones.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted routing, matrix and isochrone calculation.
entries.not_for: Java-based; some features are in the commercial offering.

entries.name: H3
entries.use_for: Index and aggregate locations on a hierarchical hexagonal grid.
entries.why: Uber's hex grid system with bindings for most languages; widely used for spatial aggregation.
entries.summary: Hexagonal hierarchical geospatial indexing system that subdivides into finer hexagonal grids, with bindings in many languages.
entries.best_for: Spatial aggregation and bucketing of locations.
entries.not_for: Hex cells only approximate shapes; not a routing or mapping tool.

entries.name: kepler.gl
entries.use_for: Visual exploration of large geospatial datasets, embeddable in React
entries.why: Open-source geo analysis tool built on deck.gl, usable as a React component; MIT.
entries.summary: High-performance web application and React component for exploring large geolocation datasets, built on MapLibre GL and deck.gl using Redux.
entries.best_for: Interactive visual exploration of big geodata, embeddable in React.
entries.not_for: Application-style tool with Redux state; heavy for simple map displays.

entries.name: Leaflet
entries.use_for: Add lightweight, mobile-friendly interactive maps to a web page.
entries.why: The most widely used open-source web map library (46k stars) with a huge plugin ecosystem.
entries.summary: Leaflet is an open-source JavaScript library for building interactive maps, around 40 kB of gzipped JS plus 3.2 kB of CSS. It works across desktop and mobile browsers, is extended through many plugins, and has a documented API.
entries.best_for: Adding lightweight, interactive tile-based maps with markers and layers to a website or web app, with plugins for extra features.
entries.not_for: 3D globes or WebGL rendering of very large datasets; it is a 2D browser mapping library, and map tiles come from a separate provider.

entries.name: mapcn
entries.use_for: Add themeable map components to a React app with one install command.
entries.why: Follows shadcn/ui patterns, adapts to dark mode and includes an agent skill.
entries.summary: Customisable React map components built on MapLibre GL and styled with Tailwind. It has markers, popups, routes and zoom, compass, locate and fullscreen controls. An agent skill teaches coding agents how to use it.
entries.best_for: React and shadcn/ui projects that need a clean map quickly.
entries.not_for: Commercial use on the default CARTO basemap, which needs a CARTO Enterprise licence. Switch to OpenStreetMap or another tile provider.

entries.name: MapLibre GL JS
entries.use_for: Render interactive vector-tile maps in the browser with WebGL.
entries.why: Open BSD-licensed fork of Mapbox GL JS; the default choice for vector maps without vendor lock-in.
entries.summary: Open-source, BSD-licensed GPU-accelerated library for interactive vector-tile maps, forked from Mapbox GL JS.
entries.best_for: Vector maps without vendor lock-in.
entries.not_for: Needs a tile source and style; heavier than Leaflet for simple maps.

entries.name: MapToPoster
entries.use_for: Generate minimalist map posters of any city from OpenStreetMap data with a Python script.
entries.why: One command makes a styled poster, with many colour themes and non-Latin city names supported.
entries.summary: MapToPoster is a Python script that makes minimalist map posters for any city. It geocodes the place with Nominatim, fetches streets with OSMnx and draws the result with matplotlib. You choose a theme and options from the command line, and can add new map layers in code.
entries.best_for: Printable city art and quick map graphics from code.
entries.not_for: Interactive web maps or routing. It outputs static images and depends on OpenStreetMap data and Nominatim rate limits.

entries.name: Martin
entries.use_for: Serve vector tiles from PostGIS, MBTiles and PMTiles with a fast Rust tile server.
entries.why: MapLibre's tile server (~4k stars); generates tiles from PostGIS on the fly.
entries.summary: Rust tile server that generates vector tiles on the fly from PostGIS and serves MBTiles and PMTiles.
entries.best_for: Serving vector tiles from PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
entries.not_for: Server to run; static hosting is easier with PMTiles.

entries.name: OpenLayers
entries.use_for: Build feature-rich web maps with many data formats, projections and OGC services.
entries.why: Most capable GIS-grade web map library; strong support for WMS/WFS and reprojection.
entries.summary: High-performance JavaScript mapping library for tiles, vector data and markers with many formats, projections and OGC services.
entries.best_for: GIS-grade web maps with WMS/WFS and reprojection.
entries.not_for: Steeper learning curve and larger API than Leaflet.

entries.name: OSMnx
entries.use_for: Download and analyze street networks and features from OpenStreetMap.
entries.why: Standard Python tool for OSM network analysis, built on NetworkX and GeoPandas.
entries.summary: Python package to download, model, analyze and visualize street networks and other features from OpenStreetMap.
entries.best_for: Network analysis, routing studies and urban research.
entries.not_for: Python research tool; not a production routing server.

entries.name: OSRM
entries.use_for: Run a very fast self-hosted routing engine on OpenStreetMap data.
entries.why: High-performance OSM routing (~8k stars, BSD-2) with routes, tables, map matching.
entries.summary: High-performance C++ routing engine for OpenStreetMap data with Nearest, Route, Table, Match and Trip services.
entries.best_for: Fast self-hosted routing and map matching.
entries.not_for: Requires preprocessing per profile and extra memory; dynamic costing is limited.

entries.name: PMTiles
entries.use_for: Serve map tiles from a single static file on S3 or a CDN, no tile server.
entries.why: Single-file tile archive format (~3k stars) that makes serverless maps cheap.

license_verified.note: BSD-3 for reference implementations; spec is public domain/CC0

entries.summary: Single-file archive format for tiled data hosted on S3 or a CDN, enabling serverless maps with no tile server.
entries.best_for: Cheap, zero-maintenance map hosting.
entries.not_for: Static archives need regeneration to update; no dynamic queries.

entries.name: react-map-gl
entries.use_for: Use MapLibre or Mapbox GL maps as React components.
entries.why: Most-used React map wrapper (~2.3M weekly npm downloads), from the vis.gl team behind deck.gl.
entries.summary: Suite of React components providing a React API for mapbox-gl or maplibre-gl.
entries.best_for: React apps using MapLibre or Mapbox maps.
entries.not_for: React only wrapper; Mapbox GL usage needs a token.

entries.name: ShadowBroker
entries.use_for: Self-host a real-time map that combines 60+ public feeds: aircraft, ships, satellites and events.
entries.why: 40+ toggleable layers, a recon toolkit and no accounts or product telemetry.
entries.summary: A self-hosted map dashboard built with Next.js, MapLibre GL and FastAPI. It merges aircraft, ships, satellites, conflict, cyber-threat and other feeds, with country dossiers and entity-graph expansion. Run with Docker Compose.
entries.best_for: Forking or studying a multi-feed geospatial OSINT interface.
entries.not_for: A library to embed. It is an application under AGPL-3.0, and some feeds depend on third-party data and keys.

entries.name: Shapely
entries.use_for: Manipulate and analyse planar geometries in Python.
entries.why: Standard Python geometry library (GEOS bindings) underlying GeoPandas.
entries.summary: Python library for manipulating and analysing planar geometries, based on GEOS.
entries.best_for: Geometry operations in Python and as a base for GeoPandas.
entries.not_for: Planar only, with no spherical geometry or data I/O.

entries.name: Supercluster
entries.use_for: Cluster huge numbers of map points quickly in the browser or Node.
entries.why: Very fast point clustering used by MapLibre/Mapbox; ISC-licensed.
entries.summary: Very fast JavaScript point clustering for browsers and Node, tested with millions of points.
entries.best_for: Clustering large marker sets on maps.
entries.not_for: Points only and static data; no UI.

entries.name: Terraink
entries.use_for: Generate printable city map posters from OpenStreetMap data, or study how such a poster tool is built.
entries.why: Themes, layer styling and typography controls with PNG, PDF and layered SVG export.
entries.summary: Terraink makes custom city map posters for any location using OpenStreetMap data. You search a place, pick or build a color theme, style roads, water, parks and buildings, then export a print-ready PNG, PDF or layered SVG. It is a React, Vite and MapLibre web app.
entries.best_for: You want to fork or learn from a map-poster web app built on OpenStreetMap and MapLibre.
entries.not_for: Still in development. AGPL-3.0 with trademark protections, so forks must rename and follow copyleft. A finished app, not a reusable library.

entries.name: Tile38
entries.use_for: Store moving objects and trigger realtime geofence events.
entries.why: Purpose-built in-memory geospatial DB with geofencing webhooks and a Redis-like protocol.
entries.summary: In-memory geolocation data store, spatial index and realtime geofencing server with Nearby, Within and Intersects queries.
entries.best_for: Tracking moving objects and triggering geofence events.
entries.not_for: In-memory, so memory-bound; not a general-purpose database.

entries.name: tippecanoe
entries.use_for: Build vector tilesets from large GeoJSON and other datasets.
entries.why: Maintained fork of Mapbox's tippecanoe by Felt; the standard tool for making vector tiles.
entries.summary: Builds vector tilesets from large GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf or CSV data.
entries.best_for: Preparing data for vector tile maps.
entries.not_for: CLI tool with no tile serving; self-hosted API version requires contacting Felt.

entries.name: Turf
entries.use_for: Run geospatial analysis (buffers, distances, intersections) on GeoJSON in JS.
entries.why: The standard modular geospatial analysis library for browser and Node.
entries.summary: Modular geospatial analysis for JavaScript on GeoJSON: buffers, distances, intersections and more.
entries.best_for: Client or server geospatial calculations in JS.
entries.not_for: In-memory GeoJSON; not for very large datasets or databases.

entries.name: Valhalla
entries.use_for: Self-host multimodal routing, isochrones and map matching on OSM data.
entries.why: Flexible OSM routing engine (~6k stars, MIT) with dynamic costing and transit.
entries.summary: Open-source routing engine on OSM data with multimodal routing, isochrones, map matching and dynamic costing.
entries.best_for: Flexible self-hosted routing with transit and custom costing.
entries.not_for: Complex setup and tile build; heavier than OSRM for basic car routing.

entries.name: World Monitor
entries.use_for: Fork or self-host a real-time world dashboard with news briefs, a 3D globe and live data layers.
entries.why: Dual map engine (globe.gl and deck.gl), many data panels and a Tauri desktop build from one codebase.
entries.summary: World Monitor is a TypeScript dashboard that combines curated news feeds, AI-written briefs, a 3D globe and flat WebGL map, and panels for markets and disasters. It runs locally with no environment variables and can use Ollama. Self-hosting uses Vercel, Docker or static builds.
entries.best_for: You want a starting point for a situational-awareness or monitoring dashboard with maps and feeds.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0, so modified hosted versions must share source. It is a finished app, not a charting or map library. Some data sources need keys.
